newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto calls on military to safeguard polls.
newsitem.headline: Suharto calls on military to safeguard polls.

text.p: President Suharto called on Indonesia's armed forces on Saturday to help safeguard general elections next year from possible disruption.

Speaking at an Armed Forces Day parade, Suharto said that in general, the country faced no major problems. But there was "unrest in various social and political organisations" that could disturb the polls due in May next year.
"To all armed force members, I ask you to prepare as well as possible to safeguard the election," Suharto said.
He added, however, that the police should handle domestic security problems. "Only if it is necessary should military units be involved," he said.
Suharto conceded there was dissatisfaction in the country over the uneven distribution of wealth.

"Dissatisfaction can be positive if it becomes a source of motivation to work harder and improve all things that are not good," he said. "On the other hand, it can also become negative if dissatisfaction becomes an issue of jealousy to spread hatred..."
The government has warned that there could be a communist resurgence and has blamed the July riots in Jakarta on a small, left-wing activist group, the People's Democratic Party (PRD).

The riots began after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party to evict supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri, who had been ousted as party leader at a government-backed, rebel congress in June.
Suharto said on Saturday there were groups that chose a negative approach and were clearly a risk to the country's security. He made no specific reference to any threat of a communist revival.
The Indonesian Communist Party was banned after an abortive 1965 coup attempt that led to the deaths of an estimated 500,000 people and to Suharto's rise to power.

The annual armed forces parade featured bands and marching troops, a parachute jump and a fly past by U.S.-made F-16 fighters and newly-arrived British Hawk aircraft. A colourful, hour-long pageant depicted Indonesian history from the Dutch colonial period through independence.
